🔴 THE FDA DIALOG STATES TWO THINGS THAT ARE NOT TRUE, on the launch path, to a customer. (a) It opens with "System Settings is open at Full Disk Access." -- System Settings was NOT opened. Measured live by Andy on the v1.0.44 upgrade walk 2026-08-24 ~18:13 HKT at step 26/37; he had to open it himself. The copy asserts a state of the world instead of establishing it. (b) It says "Find 'Ostler' in the list" and the helper adds "Ostler is already listed" -- but the actual Full Disk Access entry is named "OstlerAssistant". A customer scanning for "Ostler" can conclude it is absent and go hunting in Finder, which the same helper text tells them not to do. (c) UNADJUDICATED THIRD LIMB: Andy found the switch ALREADY ON and toggled it off/on before Done -- the known workaround for a TCC grant that survives by name but no longer matches a replaced binary. If confirmed, the instruction 'switch it on' is wrong for the upgrade path and must read 'off, then on'. Why it matters beyond wording: this is the gate for ongoing ingest. A customer who clicks Done without a real grant gets the #851 shape -- the graph silently stops growing, no error surfaced. FIX: open the pane before claiming it is open (assert ordering in a test); derive the name in the copy from the real bundle name with a test that fails when they diverge; adjudicate (c) on a box.

🟠 THE INSTALLER RE-ASKS THE iPHONE/TAILSCALE SETUP ON AN UPGRADE, a question the disk already answers. Andy, mid-walk 2026-08-24: 'that should've already been done last install time, no?' -- he is right. Measured on the box: ~/.ostler/tailscale/tailscaled.state is 2,863 bytes dated 2026-08-21T12:02:43Z, and tailscaled was already running before the walk began. MECHANISM: install.sh calls the prompt UNCONDITIONALLY at lines 8338 and 19596 (gui_read ... TAILSCALE_CONFIRM choice setup/skip). A detection branch does exist at 19718 (MSG_OK_TAILSCALE_ALREADY_INSTALLED) but it tests whether the BINARY is installed, not whether the tailnet STATE exists -- the weaker of the two questions is the only one asked. Distinct from #846 (batch the prompts): this is not 'ask at a better time', it is 'do not ask what the disk already answers'. An upgrade that re-interrogates the user about settled state reads as a reinstall. CLOSING CONDITION: prompt skipped or reduced to a one-line confirmation when a valid tailscaled.state exists AND the backend reports logged-in; guarded BOTH ways -- state present => not asked, state absent => asked. A skip proved only by the present-state arm is not proved. ⚠️ NOT MEASURED: 'the login is still valid' rests on the state file's existence and date; tailscale status --json would not return parseable output over SSH.

🟠 A RUN THAT ABORTED AT A STEP REPORTS ZERO FAILED STEPS, plus an unguarded external binary on the customer path. From the v1.0.43 walk log on the Mini, run 2026-08-24T04:40:06Z: '[gui-marker] DONE status=fail code=ERR-99-INSTALL-ABORT-L2151 failed_steps=0' and again at L1722 -- the install died INSIDE step fda_extract and the failed-step counter recorded nothing. Any consumer reading failed_steps rather than status sees a clean run. Same family as #774, where marker and STEP_END were written from different rc values; that fix made those two agree but the ABORT path evidently never increments the counter at all. SECOND, SMALLER: 'install.sh: line 9979: convert: command not found' -- ImageMagick is absent and nothing guards the call, so a raw shell error lands in the customer-visible transcript. Do NOT fix that by installing ImageMagick in the installer; guard it with a stated degradation or drop the dependency. CLOSING CONDITION: an abort inside a step records that step as failed, proved by a test that aborts mid-step and asserts failed_steps>=1.

🔴🔴 ANDY'S NAMED ITEM, ~10 DMGs UNFIXED, 'this next time without fail'. The wiki navigation bar renders with the top of its labels sliced off inside the app. ⚠️ THIS ROW'S PREVIOUS DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG IN ITS DOMINANT TERM AND IS SUPERSEDED. It blamed a CM044-internal sticky overlap (.md-header and .md-tabs both sticky at top:0, tabs sliding under the header on scroll). That is a real second-order effect but it is NOT what Andy was seeing, and chasing it is why ten DMGs of wiki-side fixes all measured correct while the defect survived: THE 56px IS TAKEN BY THE HOST, BEFORE THE WIKI GETS A SAY. ostler-assistant web/src/pages/Wiki.tsx crops the iframe with marginTop:-56px under an overflow-hidden wrapper and inflates height to calc(100% + 56px) to compensate. It was added as R3 (v1.0.13.2) to hide the wiki's own 'Andypedia' bar -- but CM044 was ALREADY hiding its header when embedded, so the 56px never covered 'Andypedia'; it ate the TAB ROW underneath. MEASURED on the built bundle: .md-header 76.8px = __inner 38.4 + .md-tabs 38.4; a 56px crop lands 17.6px INSIDE the tabs and removes 45.9% of that row; control with the crop at 0 gives 0.0%. THE FIX IS TWO REPOS AND NEITHER HALF IS SAFE ALONE: (i) CM044 #256, MERGED 6b0492d, makes the embedded page emit ONE chrome band -- __inner hidden, drawer toggle relocated into the tab row -- so there is nothing left to hide; (ii) ostler-assistant #340, MERGED 2026-08-24T16:12:25Z as e83d1997 and on oa main, removes the crop. ⚠️ THIS ROW SAID '#340, OPEN AND HELD' AND THAT WAS TRUE FOR ABOUT FIFTEEN MINUTES: the row was written before the merge. The hold is DISCHARGED on the oa side, which changes which mistake is now reachable. Both halves being unmerged was a symmetric risk; it is not symmetric any more. Ship (ii) without (i)'s image and the 'Andypedia' black bar returns (c638a6d7). 🔴 ONLY ONE WRONG SHIP IS STILL REACHABLE, AND IT IS THE OLD PIN. (ii) is on oa main, so any cut from here already carries the crop removal. Cutting v1.0.45 with the OLD wiki-site pin therefore lands 'oa fix + old image' and the c638a6d7 'Andypedia' bar returns. The other direction, an image without the oa fix, is no longer reachable by accident and is recorded here only so the reasoning survives: 🔴 SHIPPING (i)'s IMAGE WITHOUT (ii) WOULD BE WORSE THAN TODAY: post-#256 the embedded chrome is 38.4px, so a 56px crop eats the ENTIRE tab row PLUS 17.6px of page content, where today's crop at least leaves 20.8px of tabs visible. THEY MUST RIDE THE SAME CUT. 🔴 THE PREVIOUS CLOSING CONDITION'S LIMB (4) WAS IN THE WRONG COMPARTMENT AND MUST NOT BE REUSED: it asked that 'the rendered embed-mode page shows the first nav tab's top edge inside the viewport at scrollY=30', but that is measured by CM044's own harness rendering the wiki BY ITSELF in embed mode. That harness cannot see a crop applied by the host that embeds it, so limb (4) can read GREEN on every future cut while the customer still sees a clipped nav. An acceptance criterion that is structurally blind to the dominant cause is worse than none, because it terminates the search. CLOSING CONDITION, REPLACED: (1) CM044's scripts/verify_nav_bar_render.py is INVOKED from the CM044 compile and from the cut path, not merely present; (2) playwright and mkdocs are DECLARED dependencies so CANNOT-RUN cannot become the permanent resting state; (3) its --self-test is run and demonstrated RED on the reverted stylesheet and GREEN on the current one, both arms in the same run; (4) REPLACES the old limb 4 -- the COMPOSED surface is measured: the wiki rendered INSIDE the host wrapper, asserting the first tab's top edge is inside the visible box. Until that harness exists, the fallback is an assertion that the host's crop is ZERO (oa Wiki.test.tsx 'the host does not crop the embedded wiki', which asserts the frame is neither offset nor inflated and is RED-proved against the restored crop); (5) the wiki image shipped by the cut is rebuilt from CM044 main at or after 6b0492d, and the frontend shipped by the cut contains oa #340. A green from a gate whose dependencies are optional does not satisfy this row.

column1: 🔴🔴 THE INSTALLER TOLD THE CUSTOMER THE DOCTOR WAS RUNNING AND IT WAS NOT -- BUILT, PR OPEN. On Andy's v1.0.44 walk (2026-08-24) install.sh printed 'Ostler Doctor running at http://localhost:8089/doctor' while com.ostler.doctor was NOT LOADED and :8089 answered 000. Six customer surfaces were dark behind that one line -- Preferences toggles, Governor, Doctor>Channels, People, Timeline, every status header -- and the install log recorded a clean run. The wiki in the SAME app was serving 6,932 people, so the data was never the problem; only the claim was. TWO independent reasons the shape cannot be trusted: (1) 'launchctl bootstrap … || launchctl load … || true' then a bare ok -- the || true terminates the chain so there is no path that does NOT print success; (2) even without it, 'launchctl load' on a missing plist prints 'Load failed: 5' to stderr and EXITS 0 (measured macOS 26.5.2), so 'if bootstrap || load; then ok; else warn' is also unconditionally true and its else has never once run. TWELVE sites shipped this; the HAND INVENTORY FOUND ELEVEN and the predicate found the twelfth (ical-server, which printed …FAILED and then …INSTALLED on the same failure, one line apart) -- that miss is the argument for a gate rather than twelve fixes. BUILT as CM051 #1018, branch fix/launchagent-success-must-be-verified-876, commit 2291cbba: one helper _ostler_launchagent_load_verified (defined L954, before all twelve call sites) that boots out, bootstraps, falls back to load, and THEN asks launchd 'launchctl print gui/<uid>/<label>'; five new MSG_WARN_* strings for failure branches that had none; Doctor branch also sets HEALTHY=false. CLOSING CONDITION, ALL FOUR LIMBS: (1) PR #1018 MERGED to CM051 main; (2) the shipped artefact's install.sh contains the helper AND launchctl print -- proved by capability doctor_load_is_verified, not by the PR being green; (3) the class gate tests/test_launchagent_success_requires_verification.sh is INVOKED by .github/workflows/launchagent-success-verification.yml on a run that actually executed -- count invocations, not mentions (#757); (4) on the NEXT box walk, either the Doctor answers :8089 or the installer says it did not load. A green CI on an unmerged branch satisfies NONE of these.
